entries.name: ShroudOnConsoleInput
entries.signature: ShroudOnConsoleInput(inputType: string, sourcePlayer: string, message: string)

entries.name: ShroudGetPlayerName
entries.returns: string, the local player's display name; "none" when there is no local player.

entries.name: ShroudGetPlayerCombatMode
entries.returns: boolean, true while the player is in combat, otherwise false (also false when there is no player).

entries.name: ShroudGetPlayerOrientation
entries.returns: number, the player's facing as the rounded Y euler angle in degrees (0 to 360); 0 when there is no player.

entries.name: ShroudGetStatCount
entries.returns: number, the total count of stat slots (the size of the stat enum). Valid stat indices are 0 .. count-1.
entries.notes: This is the full slot count, not the count of readable stats. Many slots are hidden from Lua, so iterating all of them will still hit sentinels on the hidden ones.

entries.name: ShroudGetStatValueByNumber
entries.returns: number, the stat value; -999 (InvalidStatResult) when there is no player, the index is out of range, or the stat is hidden from Lua.

entries.name: ShroudGetStatNameByNumber
entries.returns: string, the stat's internal enum name (for example Strength); "INVALID" when there is no player, the index is out of range, or the stat is hidden.
entries.notes: This is the code name. Use ShroudGetStatDescriptionByNumber for the localized label.

entries.name: ShroudGetStatDescriptionByNumber
entries.returns: string, the stat's localized display name; "INVALID" when there is no player, the index is out of range, or the stat is hidden.

entries.name: ShroudGetStatValueByName
entries.returns: number, the stat value; 0.0 when the name is a real stat but hidden from Lua; -999 (InvalidStatResult) when there is no player or the name is unknown.
entries.notes: The two failure cases differ. A hidden-but-real stat returns 0.0, so treat 0.0 as "not readable" rather than a true zero when the stat could be hidden.

entries.name: ShroudGetBuffCount
entries.returns: number, the count of active character effects on the player; 0 when there is no player or no effects.
entries.notes: This counts raw effect entries, which is the index space for ShroudGetBuffName, ShroudGetBuffDescription, and ShroudGetBuffTimeRemaining. It is not the grouped-by-rune count returned by ShroudGetPlayerBuff.

entries.name: ShroudGetBuffName
entries.returns: string, the buff's rune name; "Invalid" when there is no player or the index is out of range.
entries.notes: The sentinel here is "Invalid" (mixed case), unlike the stat functions which use "INVALID".

entries.name: ShroudGetBuffDescription
entries.returns: string, the buff's localized display name; "Invalid" when there is no player, the index is out of range, or the effect has no display name.

entries.name: ShroudGetBuffTimeRemaining
entries.returns: number, seconds remaining on the effect; -1 when there is no player or the index is out of range.

entries.name: ShroudGetBuffIcon
entries.returns: number, a texture id for the buff's real in-game skill icon (the same graphic the game's buff bar shows), usable directly with ShroudDrawTexture / ShroudDrawTextureTooltip. Returns -1 when there is no player, the index is out of range, or the rune has no skill icon (creature/NPC runes). (API v3)
entries.notes: The icon is resolved once per skill and cached, so calling this every frame is cheap. This means an addon no longer has to ship its own artwork to show recognizable buff icons.

entries.name: ShroudGetBuffTooltip
entries.returns: string, a plain-text tooltip mirroring the game's own buff bar: the skill name, the effect's description line (when it shows a tooltip), and the time remaining, each on its own line. Empty string when there is no player or the index is out of range. NGUI markup is already stripped, so it draws cleanly through the immediate-mode GUI. (API v3)
entries.notes: Pair with ShroudDrawTextureTooltip so hovering an icon tells the player which skill it is.

entries.name: ShroudGetPlayerBuff
entries.returns: list of rune tables, or nil when there is no player. Each entry is a RuneEffects table with fields RuneName (string), RuneId (number), IsDebuff (boolean), IconId (number — texture id of the real skill icon, or -1; same value as ShroudGetBuffIcon, API v3), StackCount (number), and Effects (a list of tables, each { Description, Value, CurrentDuration, TotalDuration, TotalTick }).
entries.notes: Effects are grouped by rune name, so this list is shorter than ShroudGetBuffCount when one rune applies several effect components. StackCount is the number of grouped effect entries, an upper bound on true stacks. The result is a fresh snapshot per call; build it once per frame rather than per widget.

entries.name: ShroudGetPooledAdventurerExperience
entries.returns: number, the player's unspent pooled adventurer experience; 0 when there is no player or character data.

entries.name: ShroudGetPooledProducerExperience
entries.returns: number, the player's unspent pooled producer experience; 0 when there is no player or character data.

entries.name: ShroudGetTotalAdventurerExperience
entries.returns: number, the player's total accumulated adventurer experience; 0 when there is no player or character data.

entries.name: ShroudGetTotalProducerExperience
entries.returns: number, the player's total accumulated producer experience; 0 when there is no player or character data.

entries.name: ShroudGetAttenuationAdventurerStatus
entries.returns: boolean, true if adventurer experience is currently being attenuated (a reduced XP rate), otherwise false.
entries.notes: Reports true when the last adventurer attenuation event was under 15 minutes (900 seconds) ago.

entries.name: ShroudGetAttenuationProducerStatus
entries.returns: boolean, true if producer experience is currently being attenuated, otherwise false.

entries.name: ShroudGetPetInfo
entries.returns: a PetInfo table, or nil if there is no local player or no primary pet. Fields:
entries.notes: MoveSpeed, StrengthPower, and TauntPower are read from the local player's Taming stats (TamingMoveSpeed, TamingStrength, TamingTaunt), and MoveRate is read from the local player's general movement-rate stat (MoveRate), not from the pet entity — so all four reflect your own character rather than the creature. CriticalHit is a derived percentage, not a raw stat.

entries.name: ShroudGetPetBuff
entries.returns: a list of RuneEffects tables for the active pet, or nil if there is no local player or no primary pet. An empty list means the pet has no active effects. Each RuneEffects table has:
entries.notes: this is the same shape and grouping as the player buff call; effects are grouped by rune name in first-seen order.

entries.name: ShroudHasTarget
entries.returns: boolean. true when a target is resolved and has replicated combat state, false otherwise.
entries.notes: use this as the guard before calling any other Target function; the rest return their no-target sentinels when this is false.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetName
entries.returns: string, the target's display name. "None" when there is no target.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetId
entries.returns: number, a session-local id stable while the target object lives. -1 when there is no target.
entries.notes: the value is not a persistent database id; it only serves to detect that the target changed between frames. Cache it and compare to spot a target switch.

entries.name: ShroudIsTargetDead
entries.returns: boolean. true when the current target is dead, false when it is alive or when there is no target.

entries.name: ShroudIsTargetHealthHidden
entries.returns: boolean. true while the target hides its health bar, false when the bar is visible or there is no target.
entries.notes: while this is true, ShroudGetTargetCurrentHealth reports the target's max health, matching the stock target frame. Check this before treating current health as a real value.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetCurrentHealth
entries.returns: number, the target's current health. -1 when there is no target.
entries.notes: when the target hides its health (ShroudIsTargetHealthHidden is true) this returns the max health, not the true current value, exactly as the target frame displays it.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetMaxHealth
entries.returns: number, the target's maximum health. -1 when there is no target.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetCurrentFocus
entries.returns: number, the target's current focus. -1 when there is no target.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetMaxFocus
entries.returns: number, the target's maximum focus. -1 when there is no target.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuff
entries.returns: a list (table) of buff entries, or nil when there is no target. Effects are grouped by rune name, so each entry is one rune. Each entry is a table with fields:
entries.notes: this is the grouped view. It does not line up index-for-index with ShroudGetTargetBuffCount/ShroudGetTargetBuffName, which walk the raw un-grouped effect array.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuffCount
entries.returns: number, the count of raw effect components on the target. 0 when there is no target or the target has no effects.
entries.notes: this counts the flat, un-grouped effect array that ShroudGetTargetBuffName, ShroudGetTargetBuffDescription, and ShroudGetTargetBuffTimeRemaining index into (0-based). It is generally larger than #ShroudGetTargetBuff(), which collapses effects by rune.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuffName
entries.returns: string, the rune name of that effect. "Invalid" when there is no target or index is out of range.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuffDescription
entries.returns: string, the effect's display description. "Invalid" when there is no target or index is out of range.
entries.notes: same raw-array indexing as ShroudGetTargetBuffName.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuffTimeRemaining
entries.returns: number, seconds left on that effect (time to the end of the current tick plus the remaining ticks). -1 when there is no target or index is out of range.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuffIcon
entries.returns: number, a texture id for the target buff's real skill icon (usable with ShroudDrawTexture / ShroudDrawTextureTooltip). -1 when there is no target, the index is out of range, or the rune has no skill icon. (API v3)

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetBuffTooltip
entries.returns: string, the same native-matching plain-text tooltip as ShroudGetBuffTooltip but for the current target's buff. Empty string when there is no target or the index is out of range. (API v3)

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetStatValueByNumber
entries.returns: number, the stat value. -999 (the global InvalidStatResult) when there is no target, number is out of range, the stat is never exposed, or the target is a player and the stat is not a vital.
entries.notes: player targets expose only their vitals (current/max health and focus); every other stat returns -999 for a player target. NPC and creature targets expose the full visible stat set. Stat indices match ShroudGetStatNameByNumber from the player Stats API.

entries.name: ShroudGetTargetStatValueByName
entries.returns: number, the stat value. -999 (the global InvalidStatResult) when there is no target, the name is unknown, the stat is never exposed, or the target is a player and the stat is not a vital.
entries.notes: same player-target vitals-only rule as ShroudGetTargetStatValueByNumber. Unlike the player ShroudGetStatValueByName, a hidden-but-known stat here returns -999, not 0.

entries.name: ShroudGetDescriptionUnderMouse
entries.returns: string. The full tooltip text — the title line, then the body when the tooltip has one, joined with a newline. Markup is stripped and the text is trimmed. Returns "" when nothing readable is under the cursor.
entries.notes: For a world entity (player, NPC, item, container, object) the description falls back to the name when the entity carries no body text, so it is never empty while an entity is hovered. Resolved once per frame and shared with the other three getters.

entries.name: ShroudGetNameUnderMouse
entries.returns: string. The title line only — item name, interact text, NPC or scene name. Markup stripped and trimmed. Returns "" when nothing readable is under the cursor.
entries.notes: Live NPCs and other players carry no tooltip, so their name is read from the entity's display name instead of a tooltip title.

entries.name: ShroudGetKindUnderMouse
entries.returns: string, one of "player", "npc", "item", "container", "deco", "object", "ui", or "none" when nothing is under the cursor. A world object that matches none of the specific kinds is reported as "object", never "none".
entries.notes: Item tooltips keep the "item" kind wherever they are shown (inventory, container, vendor list, mail), not just when the item lies in the world. Precedence for world objects: player, then npc, then item, then container, then deco, then object.

entries.name: ShroudGetIdUnderMouse
entries.returns: number, a session-local id for the hovered world entity or decoration. Returns -1 when nothing is under the cursor, and also -1 for UI-sourced tooltips (an item hovered in inventory, a skill, a scene panel) where there is no world entity to identify.
entries.notes: The id is derived from the entity's runtime instance and is stable only within the current session; do not persist it or compare it across relogs. Resolved once per frame with the other three getters.

entries.name: ShroudGetPartyMemberCount
entries.returns: number, the total count of members in your party (including members not in your current scene). 0 when you are not in a party.

entries.name: ShroudGetPartyMemberName
entries.returns: string, the member's full name. "None" when no member occupies that slot or you are not in a party.
entries.notes: the name comes from the member's full character name. The in-scene health/focus getters match against the in-scene entity name, which can differ, so prefer the InScene family when reading vitals by name.

entries.name: ShroudGetPartyMemberCurrentHealth
entries.returns: number, the member's current health. -1 when you are not in a party, the slot is empty, or that member is not present in your current scene.
entries.notes: resolves the slot to a name, then looks the member up among those in your current scene, so members in another scene always return -1 even though the slot is valid.

entries.name: ShroudGetPartyMemberCountInScene
entries.returns: number, the count of party members present in your current scene. 0 when you are not in a party. This can be lower than ShroudGetPartyMemberCount when some members are in other scenes.

entries.name: ShroudGetPartyMemberNamesInScene
entries.returns: list of strings, the names of party members in your current scene. Empty when no party members are in the scene. When you are not in a party the list contains a single nil element rather than being empty, so guard for nil while iterating.
entries.notes: these names are the in-scene entity names and are the correct keys to pass to the InScene health/focus getters.

entries.name: ShroudGetPartyMemberCurrentHealthInScene
entries.returns: number, that member's current health. -1 when you are not in a party or no in-scene member matches the name.

entries.name: ShroudGetInventory
entries.returns: a list, one entry per item in the player's root inventory container. Each entry is a 14-field tuple, accessed positionally: [1] name (string, localized), [2] durability (number), [3] primary durability (number), [4] max durability (number), [5] weight (number), [6] quantity (number), [7] createdBy (string, crafter's full name, "" if none), [8] creationTime (string, date only, "" if unstamped), [9] creationSceneName (string), [10] length/size (number, fish length or pumpkin size, 0 for other items), [11] value (number, gold), [12] collectedBy (string, PvP trophy collector, "" if not a trophy), [13] collectedDate (string, "" if none), [14] collectedZone (string, "" if none). Returns nil when the player or inventory is not loaded.
entries.notes: fields 12–14 (PvP trophy provenance) are appended at the end so existing positional indexes stay stable; they are empty strings on non-trophy items.

entries.name: ShroudGetEquipments
entries.returns: a list, one entry per equipped item, each a 7-field tuple: [1] name (string, localized), [2] durability (number), [3] primary durability (number), [4] max durability (number), [5] weight (number), [6] quantity (number), [7] value (number, gold). Returns nil when the local player entity is not loaded.
entries.notes: same leading six fields as ShroudGetInventory, but the tuple ends at value; there are no creation or trophy fields.

entries.name: ShroudCurrentDeck
entries.returns: the currently equipped combat deck as an object with fields name (string, deck name), quantity (number, card count), and id (string, always ""). Returns nil when no deck is equipped or the player is not loaded.

entries.name: ShroudDeckList
entries.returns: a list of the player's decks, each an object with name (string), quantity (number, card count in that deck), and id (string, always ""). Returns nil when the player or deck data is not loaded.

entries.name: ShroudGetDeckCardList
entries.returns: a list of the deck's cards, one entry per distinct card, each an object with name (string, card display name), quantity (number, how many copies of that card are in the deck), and id (string, always ""). Returns nil when the player or deck data is not loaded.
entries.notes: duplicate cards are collapsed into one entry with an incremented quantity; locked hotbar slots are added as their own single-count entries.

entries.name: ShroudEmoteList
entries.returns: a list of string emote names the player currently owns (the same set shown in the emote UI). Returns nil when the player is not loaded or owns no emotes (the empty case yields nil, not an empty list).

entries.name: ShroudPlayEmote
entries.returns: boolean — true when the emote starts, false otherwise (throttled, emote not owned, player off the ground, or player not loaded).
entries.notes: this is the only avatar action in this group and is purely cosmetic. A 2-second throttle applies across all calls, the player must own the emote, and the avatar must be on the ground. A successful call fires the ShroudOnPlayEmote callback with the emote name.

entries.name: ShroudSwitchDeck
entries.returns: boolean — always false.
entries.notes: unimplemented stub. It performs no action and never switches decks; do not rely on it. Change decks through the game UI instead.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentSceneName
entries.returns: string, the human-readable display name of the scene at the top of the scene stack (for example Owl's Head). Never nil; an unresolved scene yields whatever the scene manager maps the id to.
entries.notes: this always reflects the real scene identity, even inside a custom-named player dungeon or basement. Use it (or the raw form) to key logic off a scene rather than the owner-supplied name. Reads the scene stack directly, so only call it once you are in a scene.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentSceneNameRaw
entries.returns: string, the internal scene id (for example PlayerDungeon_GreenBrickFoyer_3Connections), not the localized display name.
entries.notes: Same as ShroudGetCurrentSceneName but returns the stable internal id string instead of the display name. Prefer this for saved-variable keys and scene comparisons, since it does not change with client language.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentSceneOrientation
entries.returns: number, the scene's compass offset in degrees (the skybox CompassOffset). Used to align a custom compass or minimap with the scene's north.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentSceneMaxPlayerCount
entries.returns: number, the maximum number of players the current scene permits, as configured in scene data.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentSceneIsPVP
entries.returns: boolean, true if the current scene is flagged as a PVP scene, false otherwise.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentSceneIsPOT
entries.returns: boolean, true if the current scene is a Player-Owned Town, false otherwise.

entries.name: ShroudGetGameTime
entries.returns: table with the current in-game date and time. Fields: Hour (number, fractional hour of day), Day (number), Month (number), Year (number), PeriodOfDay (string, for example Morning), Season (string). When the game clock is not yet available every field is zeroed and PeriodOfDay/Season are empty strings.
entries.notes: Day and Month are the engine values plus one, so they read as human 1-based calendar numbers (the engine stores them 0-based). Hour is not offset. A zeroed table (Year 0, empty strings) means the clock was unavailable, not literal midnight of year 0.

entries.name: ShroudGetSceneCap
entries.returns: table with two number fields: Level (the adventurer level cap for the current scene) and Skill (the skill cap). Values come from the current scene's cap configuration.

entries.name: ShroudWorldToScreenPoint
entries.signature: ShroudWorldToScreenPoint(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> table
entries.returns: table with number fields x, y, z. x and y are the pixel position in screen space (origin at the bottom-left corner); z is the distance from the camera in world units. When the main camera is unavailable it returns {x = 0, y = 0, z = 0}.
entries.notes: a negative z means the world point is behind the camera, in which case the returned x/y are not a valid on-screen position. Screen-space y runs bottom-up here, unlike widget layout, whose y origin is the top; convert if you position a widget from this result.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentDungeonName
entries.returns: string, the owner-set name of the player dungeon or basement you are currently inside. Returns "" when you are outside a player dungeon or basement, or when the owner has not named it.
entries.notes: this is the only source of the custom name; the ShroudGetCurrentSceneName* functions keep returning the true scene identity.

entries.name: ShroudGetCurrentDungeonOwner
entries.returns: string, the character name of the owner of the player dungeon or basement you are inside. Returns "" when you are not inside a player dungeon or basement.
entries.notes: Same as ShroudGetCurrentDungeonName but returns the owner's character name instead of the custom area name. The owner name is present even when the area is unnamed, so it can be non-empty while the name is "".

entries.name: ShroudGetScreenX
entries.returns: number — the current screen (window) width in pixels (Screen.width).
entries.notes: reflects the live window size, so re-read it after the player resizes the window rather than storing it once at start.

entries.name: ShroudGetScreenY
entries.returns: number — the current screen (window) height in pixels (Screen.height).
entries.notes: same as ShroudGetScreenX but the vertical dimension; re-read after a resize.

entries.name: ShroudGetFullScreen
entries.returns: boolean — true if the client is running fullscreen, false if windowed (Screen.fullScreen).

entries.name: ShroudIsUIActive
entries.returns: boolean — true when the game HUD is shown, false when it is hidden (PlayerUI.showHUD).
entries.notes: use it to hide your own widgets in lockstep with the HUD (for example when the player toggles the interface off for a screenshot).

entries.name: ShroudIsCharacterSheetActive
entries.returns: boolean — true when the local player's character sheet dialog is open and shown, false when it is closed or the dialog does not exist.

entries.name: ShroudGetCharacterSheetPosition
entries.returns: two numbers x, y — the character sheet's on-screen pixel position. Returns nil when the character sheet dialog does not exist (never opened).
entries.notes: the values are pre-adjusted so you can pass them straight to widget positioning. x is measured from the left screen edge (computed as Screen.width + dialogLocalX - 44), and y is already negated to match the top-down coordinate space that ShroudSetPosition expects. Because it returns a tuple, capture both values in one call; guard against nil before using them.

entries.name: ShroudGetKeyDown
entries.returns: boolean — true for every frame the key is held down (Input.GetKey). Returns false and logs Keyname invalid: <name> to the console if keyName is not a valid KeyCode.
entries.notes: level-triggered — stays true for the whole hold. Use it for continuous actions; use ShroudGetOnKeyDown for a single edge.

entries.name: ShroudGetOnKeyDown
entries.returns: boolean — true only on the single frame the key transitions to pressed (Input.GetKeyDown). Returns false and logs Keyname invalid: <name> for an unrecognized name.
entries.notes: same as ShroudGetKeyDown but edge-triggered on press, so it fires exactly once per keystroke. Poll it from ShroudOnUpdate so you do not miss the one frame it is true.

entries.name: ShroudGetOnKeyUp
entries.returns: boolean — true only on the single frame the key transitions to released (Input.GetKeyUp). Returns false and logs Keyname invalid: <name> for an unrecognized name.
entries.notes: same as ShroudGetOnKeyDown but edge-triggered on release.

entries.name: ShroudUIPanel
entries.signature: ShroudUIPanel(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI, depth: number) -> number
entries.returns: number, the new panel's 0-based id, or -1 if textureID was given (not -1) but no texture with that id exists.
entries.notes: panels are draggable and receive mouse enter/exit callbacks by default. A panel is created with a Unity Mask component already attached, so it clips its children to its own rect without any ShroudSetMask call.

entries.name: ShroudUIImage
entries.signature: ShroudUIImage(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI, depth: number) -> number
entries.returns: number, the new image's 0-based id, or -1 if the texture id is unknown.
entries.notes: unlike a panel, an image is created without a Mask; add one with ShroudSetMask when you want it to clip its children.

entries.name: ShroudUIText
entries.signature: ShroudUIText(text: string, fontSize: number, x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI, depth: number) -> number
entries.returns: number, the new label's 0-based id. This call has no texture dependency and does not return -1.

entries.name: ShroudUIButton
entries.signature: ShroudUIButton(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI, depth: number) -> number
entries.returns: number, the new button's 0-based id, or -1 if the texture id is unknown.
entries.notes: the button wires click and enter/exit listeners; handle clicks through ShroudSetClickListener and the ShroudOnMouseClick callback.

entries.name: ShroudUIInput
entries.signature: ShroudUIInput(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI) -> number
entries.returns: number, the new input's 0-based id. No texture dependency; does not return -1.
entries.notes: starts with an italic "Enter text..." placeholder; read the field with ShroudGetInputText and set it with ShroudSetInputText.

entries.name: ShroudUIToggle
entries.signature: ShroudUIToggle(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI) -> number
entries.returns: number, the new toggle's 0-based id. No texture dependency; does not return -1.
entries.notes: read/write the checked state with ShroudGetToggle/ShroudSetToggle; state changes fire the ShroudOnToggleChange callback.

entries.name: ShroudSetPosition
entries.signature: ShroudSetPosition(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.None, id is negative, or id is out of range for that kind.

entries.name: ShroudGetPosition
entries.returns: a LuaVector2 userdata object with numeric fields x and y (accessed as pos.x / pos.y), or nil if kind is UI.None, id is negative, or id is out of range. This is a registered userdata, not a Lua table, so type(pos) is "userdata". The returned y is un-negated, so it matches the value you gave ShroudSetPosition.

entries.name: ShroudSetSize
entries.signature: ShroudSetSize(id: number, kind: UI, width: number, height: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.

entries.name: ShroudSetScale
entries.signature: ShroudSetScale(id: number, kind: UI, scale: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.

entries.name: ShroudSetPivot
entries.signature: ShroudSetPivot(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
entries.notes: as a side effect this also multiplies the widget's current anchored position by the new pivot x and y, so setting the pivot generally shifts the widget — set the pivot before positioning, then call ShroudSetPosition.

entries.name: ShroudSetAnchorMin
entries.signature: ShroudSetAnchorMin(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.

entries.name: ShroudSetAnchorMax
entries.signature: ShroudSetAnchorMax(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean

entries.name: ShroudRotateObject
entries.signature: ShroudRotateObject(id: number, kind: UI, degrees: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.

entries.name: ShroudSetColor
entries.signature: ShroudSetColor(id: number, kind: UI, hexColor: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.None or UI.Button, id is negative, or id is out of range.
entries.notes: an unparseable hex string does not fail the call — it resolves to transparent black and still returns true, so validate your color strings (and keep the #).

entries.name: ShroudSetTransparency
entries.signature: ShroudSetTransparency(id: number, kind: UI, alpha: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.None, id is negative, or id is out of range.

entries.name: ShroudModifyImage
entries.signature: ShroudModifyImage(id: number, kind: UI, textureID: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.Text, id is negative, the texture id is unknown, or id is out of range for that kind.

entries.name: ShroudModifyText
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false if id is negative or out of range for the text list.

entries.name: ShroudSetTextAlignment
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false only when id is negative.
entries.notes: this guards against a negative id but does not bounds-check the upper end — passing an id at or beyond the text-widget count throws. Only pass ids returned by ShroudUIText.

entries.name: ShroudSetFontSize
entries.signature: ShroudSetFontSize(id: number, kind: UI, size: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean, true on success; false for any other kind, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.

entries.name: ShroudSetMask
entries.returns: boolean, true if a Mask was added; false if the kind is unsupported, id is negative or out of range, or the widget already has a Mask.
entries.notes: adds a Unity Mask component so child widgets are clipped to this widget's rect. Use it to build scroll regions or clipped panels. A panel already ships with a Mask, so ShroudSetMask(panel, UI.Panel) returns false and changes nothing — panels clip their children out of the box. This call is meant for an image, which is created without a Mask; it only re-adds a Mask to a panel after one was removed with ShroudUnsetMask.

entries.name: ShroudUnsetMask
entries.returns: boolean, true if a Mask was removed; false if the kind is unsupported, id is negative or out of range, or the widget has no Mask to remove.
entries.notes: because a panel is created with a Mask, ShroudUnsetMask(panel, UI.Panel) succeeds and stops the panel from clipping its children.

entries.name: ShroudSetParent
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudSetParent(id: number, kind: UI, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number
entries.returns: number. Always -1, even on success (frozen quirk) — do not treat the return as an error code. id < 0 or parentId < 0 returns -1 with no change.
entries.notes: reparents keeping local layout (world-position-stays is false), so the child's size and anchored position are preserved relative to the new parent. Reparenting a panel under a panel removes the child's bring-to-front behavior.

entries.name: ShroudSetPanelParent
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudSetPanelParent(panelId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number
entries.returns: number. Always -1 (frozen quirk).
entries.notes: parentId = -1 reparents the panel to the root canvas and restores its bring-to-front component, which is the way to promote a nested panel back to a free-floating window.

entries.name: ShroudSetImageParent
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudSetImageParent(imageId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number

entries.name: ShroudSetTextParent
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudSetTextParent(textId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number

entries.name: ShroudSetButtonParent
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudSetButtonParent(buttonId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number

entries.name: ShroudGetParentID
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: number. The 0-based id of the parent widget, or -1 when the widget is invalid, kind is UI.None, or its parent is the root canvas rather than another addon widget.
entries.notes: the returned id is only meaningful together with ShroudGetParentObjectKind — the id indexes whichever widget list the parent belongs to, so read both to identify the parent unambiguously.

entries.name: ShroudGetParentObjectKind
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: UI. The parent widget's kind, or UI.None when the widget is invalid, kind is UI.None, or the parent is the root canvas.
entries.notes: pair with ShroudGetParentID to fully resolve the parent.

entries.name: ShroudSetDragguable
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. true when drag support was added, false for an unsupported kind, an invalid id, or a widget that is already draggable.
entries.notes: the spelling Dragguable is frozen; do not correct it. Adds pointer-drag and bring-to-front behavior. Required before ShroudSetResizable or ShroudMinMaxSize will take effect.

entries.name: ShroudUnsetDragguable
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior

entries.name: ShroudSetResizable
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudSetResizable(id: number, kind: UI, direction: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true when applied, false for a non-panel, an invalid id, or a panel that is not already draggable.
entries.notes: the panel must first be made draggable with ShroudSetDragguable; without the drag component this is a no-op that returns false.

entries.name: ShroudMinMaxSize
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudMinMaxSize(id: number, kind: UI, min: number, max: number, direction: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true when applied, false for an unsupported kind, an invalid id, or a widget that is not already draggable.
entries.notes: like ShroudSetResizable, the widget must already be draggable (ShroudSetDragguable) for the clamp to attach.

entries.name: ShroudSetInOutListener
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. true when the listener was added, false for an unsupported kind (UI.Toggle/UI.Input), an invalid id, or a widget that already has one.
entries.notes: while the listener is attached, moving the pointer onto the widget invokes your ShroudOnMouseOver(id, kind) callback and moving off invokes ShroudOnMouseOut(id, kind).

entries.name: ShroudUnsetInOutListener
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. false for UI.None/invalid id.
entries.notes: frozen quirk — the removal branch tests for the drag component, not the listener, so it only strips the listener from widgets that are not also draggable and returns false on a draggable widget. To be certain a widget stops firing over/out, destroy and recreate it rather than relying on this call for a draggable one.

entries.name: ShroudSetClickListener
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. true when the listener was added, false for an unsupported kind (UI.Toggle/UI.Input), an invalid id, or a widget that already has one.
entries.notes: while attached, releasing the pointer over the widget invokes your ShroudOnMouseClick(id, kind) callback. Useful for making a plain image or panel act like a button.

entries.name: ShroudUnsetClickListener
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. false for UI.None, an invalid id, or a UI.Text/UI.Button kind.
entries.notes: frozen quirk — the removal branch is inverted (it destroys only when no listener is present), so it does not actually strip a live click listener. To reliably stop click handling, destroy the widget with ShroudDestroyObject and recreate it.

entries.name: ShroudRaycastObject
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.signature: ShroudRaycastObject(id: number, kind: UI, enable: boolean) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true when applied, false for UI.None or an out-of-range id.
entries.notes: toggles the underlying graphic's raycast target. Disable it on a decorative overlay so it does not block the widgets beneath it.

entries.name: ShroudHideObject
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. true when the widget was deactivated, false for UI.None, an out-of-range id, or an unsupported kind (UI.Toggle/UI.Input).
entries.notes: deactivates the widget's GameObject; its children hide with it, and its id and state are retained for a later ShroudShowObject. To hide a toggle or input, parent it under a panel and hide the panel instead.

entries.name: ShroudShowObject
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior

entries.name: ShroudHideLuaUI
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. true when the addon canvas was hidden, false if no canvas exists yet.
entries.notes: deactivates the entire addon canvas at once, hiding every widget your addon created without destroying them. Pair with ShroudShowLuaUI. Use it for a global show/hide hotkey.

entries.name: ShroudShowLuaUI
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior

entries.name: ShroudDestroyObject
entries.category: UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior
entries.returns: boolean. true when the widget was destroyed, false for UI.None or an out-of-range id.
entries.notes: destroys the GameObject and nulls its slot in the widget list. The id is not renumbered — the freed slot is reused by the next widget you create of that kind, so a create call after a destroy can hand back the same id. Do not keep using an id after destroying it.

entries.name: ShroudSetButtonColor
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.signature: ShroudSetButtonColor(id: number, mode: ButtonMode, hexColor: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. false if mode is ButtonMode.None, or id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
entries.notes: there is no parse-failure return. The hex string is parsed with ColorUtility.TryParseHtmlString, but its success flag is ignored, so an unparseable string (or a bare hex value missing the leading #) does not fail the call. Instead the color is left at the default fully-transparent black (0,0,0,0), which is still applied and the call still returns true (for a valid id). Always pass a valid #-prefixed hex string and check it yourself. Each call also assigns a brand-new color block that carries only the one state you set, so the other three state colors (and the fade duration and color multiplier) reset to zero. Set every state you care about in the same pass, and expect the colors to show only when the button's transition is Transition.ColorTint.

entries.name: ShroudSetButtonImage
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.signature: ShroudSetButtonImage(id: number, mode: ButtonMode, textureID: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. false if mode is ButtonMode.None, id or textureID is negative, or the texture id is not loaded; otherwise true.
entries.notes: ButtonMode.Normal replaces the button's base Image sprite directly. Highlighted, Pressed, and Disabled go into the button's sprite state and only appear when the transition is Transition.SpriteSwap.

entries.name: ShroudSetButtonTransition
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. Returns true whenever the id is in range, and also falls through to true when transition is not one of the three valid values, so the return value is not a reliable success check.
entries.notes: the id is only bounds-checked against the upper end (id < count) with no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the button list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error), not a false return. Pass an id you got back from ShroudUIButton. Pick Transition.ColorTint before setting state colors with ShroudSetButtonColor, or Transition.SpriteSwap before setting state sprites with ShroudSetButtonImage.

entries.name: ShroudGetInputText
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: string, the full field contents. Returns nil if id is negative or out of range.
entries.notes: returns the complete value, not just the portion currently scrolled into view.

entries.name: ShroudSetInputText
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.

entries.name: ShroudSetInputContentType
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.

entries.name: ShroudSetPlaceholderText
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.

entries.name: ShroudSetInputBackgroundColor
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
entries.notes: the hex string is parsed before the # is applied, so a bare hex value without # fails to parse and leaves the color black. Always pass the leading #.

entries.name: ShroudSetInputCharacterLimit
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.

entries.name: ShroudSetInputReadonly
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.

entries.name: ShroudGetToggle
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean, the toggle's checked state (true = checked). Returns nil if id is at or past the top of the range.
entries.notes: only the upper bound is checked (id < count); there is no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the toggle list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error) rather than returning nil. Only pass ids you got back from ShroudUIToggle.

entries.name: ShroudSetToggle
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is at or past the top of the range; otherwise true.
entries.notes: only the upper bound is checked (id < count); there is no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the toggle list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error) rather than returning false. Only pass ids you got back from ShroudUIToggle.

entries.name: ShroudSetToggleReadonly
entries.category: UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles
entries.returns: boolean. false if id is at or past the top of the range; otherwise true.
entries.notes: only the upper bound is checked (id < count); there is no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the toggle list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error) rather than returning false. Only pass ids you got back from ShroudUIToggle.

entries.name: ShroudGUILabel
entries.signature: ShroudGUILabel(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, text: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. Always true; there is no failure sentinel.
entries.notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(); it draws for a single frame, so re-issue it every frame. Marked obsolete in the client and slated for removal.

entries.name: ShroudButton
entries.signature: ShroudButton(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, text: string, tooltip: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true on the frame the button is clicked, otherwise false. Also false if textureID does not resolve, so a click and a missing texture are indistinguishable from the return value alone.
entries.notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). Because a valid texture is required, load one even for a mostly-text button.

entries.name: ShroudButtonRepeat
entries.signature: ShroudButtonRepeat(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, text: string, tooltip: string) -> boolean

entries.name: ShroudDrawTexture
entries.signature: ShroudDrawTexture(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true on success, false if textureID does not resolve to a loaded texture.
entries.notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). The texture is scaled to the rect; query its native size with ShroudGetTextureSize if you need to preserve aspect ratio.

entries.name: ShroudDrawTextureTooltip
entries.signature: ShroudDrawTextureTooltip(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, text: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true on success, false if textureID does not resolve (the tooltip region is still registered).
entries.notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). Draws the texture and registers its hover region in one call. The host renders the tooltip after every addon's ShroudOnGUI, so it always sits above the icons. When rects overlap, the last one drawn under the cursor wins.

entries.name: ShroudGUITooltip
entries.signature: ShroudGUITooltip(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, text: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. Always true.
entries.notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). Registers a hover region without drawing anything, so you can attach a tooltip to something you drew yourself (a ShroudGUILabel, a widget, an empty area). Registration lasts one GUI pass; re-issue it every frame.

entries.name: ShroudLoadTexture
entries.notes: loading the same file path twice returns the same handle (results are cached by path, case-insensitive). The default wrap mode is Repeat; use ShroudSetTextureClamp to switch it to Clamp.

entries.name: ShroudLoadSound
entries.notes: the load runs asynchronously on a coroutine. The clip is appended to the sound list only when the web request completes, so its playable id (its 1-based position in that list) is assigned by load-completion order. Poll ShroudListSound to find loaded clips before calling ShroudPlaySound. Decode errors are logged, not returned.

entries.name: ShroudListSoundReset
entries.notes: after a reset, clip ids restart from 1 as new clips load.

entries.name: ShroudPlaySound
entries.notes: there are five playback channels. The returned index is 0-based, but ShroudStopSound and ShroudIsChannelPlaying take a 1-based channel, so add 1 before passing it back. Playing a sound also fires the addon's ShroudOnPlaySound callback with the clip name.

entries.name: ShroudStopFX
entries.notes: the call also prunes destroyed effects from the tracked list as a side effect.

entries.name: ShroudConsoleLog
entries.notes: writes a chat entry of type LuaMessage with ForceVisible = false, so it appears in the chat log but does not force the chat window open. The un-prefixed alias ConsoleLog is registered to the same function.

entries.name: ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint
entries.notes: this sets Script.DefaultOptions.DebugPrint, which is process-wide, so it changes print routing for every loaded addon, not just yours. The default at startup is the chat console (true).

entries.name: print
entries.notes: this host overrides the stock print. Output is routed through Script.DefaultOptions.DebugPrint, which by default is the Lua chat console, so print writes to in-game chat like ShroudConsoleLog. ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(false) redirects it to the player-invisible engine log; ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(true) restores chat output. The routing is shared by all addons.

entries.name: collectgarbage
entries.signature: collectgarbage(mode: string, arg: number) -> number | boolean | (number, number) | nil
entries.returns: depends on mode — "collect"/"restart"/absent run a full blocking collect and return the number 0; "count" returns two numbers (managedKB, bytesMod1024) from the managed heap; "step" returns a boolean that is true when the collection cycle is complete; "isrunning" returns a boolean; any other mode ("stop", "setpause", "setstepmul", ...) returns nil.
entries.notes: this replaces MoonSharp's stock collectgarbage (#914). Modes that would let an addon disable the GC shared by the whole client are intentionally no-ops returning nil. "step" never falls back to a blocking collect; when incremental GC is unavailable it self-guards and reports complete. Prefer "step" over the blocking "collect" to avoid a 140–190ms stall.

entries.name: ShroudForceGC
entries.notes: runs a full, blocking Gen2 GC.Collect(), which can stall the client for roughly 140–190ms. Prefer collectgarbage("step") for incremental collection; use this only when a hard, immediate collect is genuinely needed.

entries.name: ShroudRegisterPeriodic
entries.signature: ShroudRegisterPeriodic(name: string, functionName: string, period: number, repeating: boolean) -> boolean
entries.notes: the target is resolved by name, so define the function as a global before calling this. The callback takes no parameters — read whatever state it needs from the API directly.

entries.name: ShroudListPeriodics
entries.notes: the value is a MoonSharp enumerator over the names, so drive it with a generic for as shown. Names appear in scheduled-time order.

entries.name: ShroudLoadInkVariable
entries.returns: the stored value as a string, or nil when no value is stored, when varName is not a non-empty string, or when no character is logged in.
entries.notes: existence is exact — a value that was saved as an empty string, or the literal "null" the Ink side treats as its own unsaved sentinel, still comes back as a string, not nil.

entries.name: ShroudSaveInkVariable
entries.signature: ShroudSaveInkVariable(varName: string, value: string | number | boolean) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true on success; false when varName is not a non-empty string, when no character is logged in, when the value type is not string/number/boolean, when a string exceeds 8192 characters, or when a number is NaN or infinite.
entries.notes: the write is not flushed to disk immediately (parity with the Ink side, and to avoid main-thread I/O from an addon writing every frame); Unity persists it on a clean quit. A conversation in progress sees the new value only at its next loadVariable.

entries.name: ShroudHasInkVariable
entries.returns: boolean. true only when a value is stored for this character under varName; false when nothing is stored, when varName is not a non-empty string, or when no character is logged in.

entries.name: ShroudDeleteInkVariable
entries.returns: boolean. true when a stored value existed and was removed; false when nothing was stored, when varName is not a non-empty string, or when no character is logged in.

entries.name: ShroudSetSavedVar
entries.signature: ShroudSetSavedVar(key: string, value: string|number|boolean|table|nil, scope: string) -> boolean
entries.returns: boolean. true when the value was stored (table marked dirty) — a nil value counts as stored and returns true — false on an invalid key or a non-persistable value type.
entries.notes: does not write to disk. It updates the in-memory table and marks it dirty; the file is written on the next flush trigger (logout, disable/unload, quit, or ShroudFlushSavedVars). Character scope is keyed by the current character, so the same key holds independent values on different characters.

entries.name: ShroudGetSavedVar
entries.returns: the stored value with its original Lua type (string, number, boolean, or table), or nil if the key is unset, the key is invalid, or no saved-variable table exists yet for that addon and scope.
entries.notes: a stored table is returned by reference to the in-memory copy; mutating its fields changes the cached value, but you still must call ShroudSetSavedVar (or otherwise mark the table dirty) for the change to be flagged for the next flush.

entries.name: ShroudDeleteSavedVar
entries.returns: boolean. true when the key existed and was removed (table marked dirty), false on an invalid key, a missing table, or a key that was not present.
entries.notes: like the setter, this only marks the table dirty; the deletion reaches disk on the next flush.

entries.name: ShroudFlushSavedVars
entries.returns: boolean. true if every dirty addon table was written (also true when nothing was dirty), false if any file failed to write or a table exceeded the 256 KB serialized limit.
entries.notes: forces an immediate write of all pending changes rather than waiting for logout, disable/unload, or quit. A table whose JSON exceeds 256 KB is skipped, not written, and logs a size-limit message to the addon console; the call then returns false.

entries.name: ShroudPlayerX
entries.returns: Local player world X position

entries.name: ShroudPlayerY
entries.returns: Local player world Y position

entries.name: ShroudPlayerZ
entries.returns: Local player world Z position

entries.name: ShroudPlayerCurrentHealth
entries.returns: Local player current health

entries.name: ShroudPlayerCurrentFocus
entries.returns: Local player current focus

entries.name: ShroudPlayerGold
entries.returns: Local player gold total

entries.name: ShroudTime
entries.returns: Engine time in seconds since start (Time.time)

entries.name: ShroudDeltaTime
entries.returns: Frame delta in seconds, clamped at the Maximum Allowed Timestep (~0.1 s). Use this to pace animation

entries.name: ShroudRealDeltaTime
entries.returns: Unclamped wall-clock frame delta in seconds; reflects the true length of a stall

entries.name: ShroudServerTime
entries.returns: Server UTC time, formatted as a string (updated once per whole second)

entries.name: ShroudMouseX
entries.returns: Mouse X in pixels

entries.name: ShroudMouseY
entries.returns: Mouse Y in pixels, top-left origin (screenHeight - mouseY)

entries.name: ShroudLuaApiVersion
entries.returns: Current API version. Presently 3

entries.name: ShroudLuaPath
entries.returns: Absolute path to the addon's Lua folder

entries.name: ShroudDataPath
entries.returns: Absolute path to the addon data folder

entries.name: InvalidStatResult
entries.returns: The numeric failure sentinel, -999. Stat/value getters return this when a value is hidden or the query is invalid
